clue.text: Insect hovering around door maybe causing rage

parts.note: a fly is a common winged insect
an insect hovering near a door's knob is literally off the handle, a door being one example of something with a handle

explanation.surface: A bluebottle buzzing round the front door drives someone to fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is read literally: hovering near a door is being off (away from) the handle. 'causing' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for losing one's temper suddenly, so it works as a verb for flaring up in fury.

clue.text: Football people cross supporting United — dad's mistake

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: the FA, the Football Association, runs English football
U is a standard abbreviation for United in team names
a cross is the letter X
pa's is an informal word for dad's

explanation.surface: A football official crossing a United fan makes the dad's blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' looks like fandom but places X under U in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for a social blunder or embarrassing slip, a synonym for an error of manners.

clue.text: Eccentric hobby is not polite

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of the following words are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Someone's odd pastime is considered rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving like a lout or hooligan is the opposite of courteous, so a synonym for impolite and boorish.

clue.text: Official in black who regularly sends people off

definitions.text: Official in black who regularly sends people off

parts.words: Official in black who regularly sends people off
parts.note: reads like a football referee in black kit sending players off, but describes the undertaker who dresses in black and sends the dead off on their final journey

explanation.surface: A referee in a black kit is always showing red cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture of a referee dismissing players is the false path; 'sends off' is also seeing the dead to their burial.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker arranges burials, wears black mourning dress and sees the deceased off from this world.

clue.text: This must be detailed with each burglary?

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, so the word this loses its final letter

parts.note: each and every are synonyms

explanation.surface: A police report demanding a full account with every break-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' means having its tail cut off: THIS becomes THI. 'must be' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is the act of a thief, and breaking in to steal is burglary, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Occasionally witnessed teen's grim need for something to drive

indicators.note: seen only now and then, so just every other letter of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: An adolescent's dire wish for a car is glimpsed now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of TEENS GRIM NEED: E, N, G, I, N, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor is the machine that powers a vehicle, so it is what drives the car.

clue.text: As a bowler's jettisoned with little justification?

definitions.meaning: a bowler is a hat, so when one is dropped it is literally at its fall
on the slightest pretext, without needing a reason

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler gets dropped from the side on flimsy grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket, but here it is the hard felt hat; jettisoning it is its drop.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly and without hesitation or good reason, hence on minimal grounds.

clue.text: Head of force in demand over church security

indicators.note: the leading letter goes in the middle of the reversed word
over signals the word for demand is turned around

parts.note: to need something is to demand it

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A police chief, much sought after, oversees the security of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the word for demand around to give DEEN, and 'in' puts the F inside it, making DEFEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Protection from attack is security, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Most natural in Spain — snooze showing bottom on top!

parts.note: E is the international vehicle registration letter for Spain (España)

indicators.note: in a down entry, the bottom letter of the word for snooze is brought up to the top

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon nap in Spain

explanation.surface: Nothing comes more naturally in Spain than an afternoon nap, flat on one's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' and 'top' are the ends of this down entry, so the nap's last letter moves up front; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Simplest, least effortful, coming without strain: the superlative for what comes most readily.

clue.text: Inflexible international organisation British close

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations
a close is an end or ending

explanation.surface: The United Nations and Britain conclude a rigid agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Not bending means rigid and refusing to yield, so a synonym for stiff or unyielding.

clue.text: Rows hard, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for hard is sent to the end

parts.note: stiff means hard or rigid

explanation.surface: Rowers pull hard from the first stroke to the last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' suggests rowing a boat but means quarrels (rhymes with cows).
explanation.definitionFit: Minor quarrels or spats are rows, so the plural nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Earlier church official

definitions.meaning: the head of a monastery or a deputy to an abbot

explanation.surface: A clergyman from an earlier time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for previous and a noun for a monastic superior below an abbot.

clue.text: Ace evening with no one spreading retribution

indicators.note: spreading means scattering the letters across a new order
with no signals that a letter is to be left out of the mix

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A superb night out without a single person spreading spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no one' removes I from ACE EVENING; 'spreading' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Punishment inflicted in return for a wrong is revenge, the same idea as retribution.

clue.text: They learn of the sun's trapping carbon and hydrogen

indicators.note: trapping means holding other letters inside

parts.note: solar means of the sun, and the 's is kept as S
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Students of the sun capture its carbon and hydrogen, a chemistry lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned people and students are those who study, so the plural noun matches those who learn.

clue.text: In France nothing is put in to back the East

indicators.note: the French word goes inside the other piece
back means the little word to is read in reverse

parts.note: rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: In France nothing is done to support the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the little word around to give OT, which then holds the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is a traditional name for Asia and the lands east of Europe.

clue.text: Criminal bail a nun furnishes once in six months?

indicators.note: criminal suggests these letters have been wrongly treated and rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook posts bail for a nun to cover a half-yearly event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furnishes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening twice a year means occurring every half-year, one recurrence in each six-month period.

clue.text: Nanny's gold shoes, perhaps

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
shoes come as a pair, an example of a set of two

explanation.surface: A nanny's golden pair of shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nanny's' is the definition plus 's for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A young foreign helper living with a family to mind children, a kind of live-in childminder.

clue.text: 'Heart of Moral Man' a cert for book of the year

indicators.note: the heart of the phrase holds the letters, buried inside its words

explanation.surface: A title called Heart of Moral Man is tipped to be book of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are inside moRAL MAN A Cert.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual reference publication with calendars, tides and the year's events, literally a book for one year.

clue.text: Longin' to steal thousand grand and drink to celebrate?

indicators.note: to steal means taking letters into it

parts.note: pinin' is longing with its last letter dropped, like the clue's own clipped word
K is a thousand, from kilo
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone yearning to pinch a fortune and toast it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Longin'' drops its G, so the synonym does too: PININ'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin cocktail with angostura bitters, here imagined as a drink raised in celebration of being in the pink.

clue.text: Detective's area is murder

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, with the 's kept as S
a patch is an area, such as a police beat

explanation.surface: A detective's beat is a murder case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill someone off efficiently is to finish them, a verb sense for slaying.

clue.text: Guitarist's effect, lot more distorted

indicators.note: distorted means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guitarist adds more and more distortion to the sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' looks like guitar distortion, but here it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A wavering pitch or volume effect, produced on electric guitar with a whammy bar.

clue.text: One giving party among toffs' set, so hard up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
among says the letters lie inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A party-giver mixes with posh folk, though she is so broke.
explanation.walkthrough: Backwards, toffS SET SO Hard gives the answer; 'hard up' looks like 'poor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who entertains guests at her own gathering is the one throwing the party.

clue.text: Star's bedtime

parts.note: the sun is a star, and the hour it goes to rest below the horizon is its bedtime

explanation.surface: When a celebrity turns in for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity; it is our own star.
explanation.definitionFit: The time of evening when the sun goes down, imagined as the hour it retires for the night.

clue.text: Model that's still on display

parts.note: a model that stays motionless in a shop window is a dummy for showing clothes

explanation.surface: A fashion model is still being shown off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as 'even now' but means 'motionless'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy figure used to show clothes in a shop window, a model that never moves.

clue.text: Heard insects in leaves

indicators.note: heard signals that the word for the insects is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: fleas are small jumping insects

explanation.surface: Insects heard rustling in the leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away from danger is to depart in haste, so a synonym for goes off.

clue.text: King eludes one of his followers in darkness

indicators.note: eludes means slips away from, so the letter for king leaves the word

parts.note: a knight serves a king, and is also a chess piece
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch gives one of his retainers the slip after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours when the sun is down and it is dark, a synonym for darkness.

clue.text: Where a map-reader's only way is up

definitions.text: Where a map-reader's only way is up

parts.words: Where a map-reader's only way is up
parts.note: on a map north is up, and at the bottom of the globe every direction is north

explanation.surface: A navigator's spot where things can only get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only way is up' sounds like optimism; at the planet's bottom every way out heads north, up the map.
explanation.definitionFit: The southernmost point of the earth, where every direction leads north, toward the top of a map.

clue.text: Wind cannot tug sailor hats off

indicators.note: to wind is to twist or coil, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A gust stops a seaman tugging at his headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like a breeze but is the verb (rhymes with find).
explanation.definitionFit: Raising one's hat in respect is a gesture of praise, so the exclamation means well done.
